title: Short Stuff: The Conch Republic
summary: Short Stuff episode on the Conch Republic. In the 1980s Key West was a major hub for marijuana and cocaine smuggling, with local officials and firefighters reportedly involved. The Reagan administration launched the South Florida Task Force Against Crime, which set up a border patrol checkpoint at Florida City that effectively cut off the Keys, causing a seventeen-mile traffic jam and hurting tourism. The Keys' people and government sued in federal court in Miami and lost. Mayor Dennis Wardlow then declared the Keys would secede, and on the next day declared Key West the independent Conch Republic, with himself as Prime Minister. A mock war ended with a surrender at a Navy base and a request for a billion dollars in aid, which the US did not give, though the checkpoint ended soon after. The hosts discuss the Conch Republic's continued celebrations each April, its passport stamps and flag, the Fifth World concept, comparisons to Sealand and The Mouse That Roared, and some Key West attractions, including the Key West Museum and a Museum of Umbrella Covers in Maine.

segments.title: Key West smuggling era
segments.summary: The hosts introduce Key West and describe its history as a smuggling hub, with marijuana and cocaine coming in from South America and Cuba, teens driving bales north to Miami, and local officials and firefighters reportedly involved.

segments.title: South Florida Task Force and Florida City checkpoint
segments.summary: The Reagan administration created the South Florida Task Force Against Crime, which cracked down on drugs in the Keys. A border patrol checkpoint at Florida City, ostensibly for migrants but actually searching for drugs, effectively cut Key West off from the mainland.
topics: South Florida Task Force Against Crime

segments.title: Traffic jam and lawsuit against the roadblock
segments.summary: The checkpoint caused a seventeen-mile traffic jam and hurt tourism, hotels, restaurants and bars. The Keys filed an injunction in federal court in Miami, which allowed the roadblock to stay.

segments.title: Secession and founding of the Conch Republic
segments.summary: Mayor Dennis Wardlow announced the Keys would secede. The next day he declared Key West an independent nation, the Conch Republic, a sovereign 'Fifth World' state of mind, and himself its Prime Minister.

segments.title: Mock war, surrender, and aid request
segments.summary: The Conch Republic declared war on the United States in a staged event ending with Cuban bread broken over a man dressed as a US naval officer. Wardlow surrendered at a Navy base and requested a billion dollars in aid, which was not given, though the roadblock soon ended.

segments.title: Conch Republic traditions: passports, flag, April celebration
segments.summary: The hosts describe the Conch Republic passport stamps, its motto flag, and the nine-day April celebration. They mention Secretary General Peter Anderson, who has died.

segments.title: Key West sights and weird museums
segments.summary: The hosts discuss Key West as a fishing and diving destination with few beaches, mention the Key West Museum with its Robert the doll and a necrophilia-related exhibit, and plug the Museum of Umbrella Covers on Peaks Island, Maine.

segments.title: Sign-off
segments.summary: The hosts close the short episode and give the standard Stuff You Should Know production credit.
